reason: No prior evidence is cited for any of the key premises; the hypothesis relies entirely on unsupported claims about Al-induced oxide formation, its tribological benefits across the full temperature range, low-temperature phase stability, and the baseline alloy's deficiencies.
premises: Adding ~5 at.% Al to CoCrFeNi promotes formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3-rich film during sliding
The Al2O3-rich film reduces friction and wear from 25 °C to 800 °C
At low temperatures, 5 at.% Al preserves original HEA phase stability
Unmodified CoCrFeNi shows inadequate passivation and increased wear at high temperatures
